news.title: ‘Weekday games were amazing’: pubs toast extra £150m in World Cup sales
news.lede: England’s progress provides best football-related uplift of recent years, with one pub too packed to host its Dolly Parton tribute. Late opening hours and England’s progress to the semi-final of an expanded World Cup helped provide the best football-related uplift of recent years for pubs, figures suggest. Pubs poured 30m extra pints over the course of the tournament compared with a normal trading period, with busy pumps delivering £150m in added sales, according to the British Beer & Pubs Association (BBPA). The World Cup-related increase in sales, as fans followed England and Scotland games, also appears to have outstripped that seen during previous competitions, including England’s run to the final of Euro 2024.

news.title: Former player and World Cup champion to join Jürgen Klopp in the German national setup
news.lede: As part of the German national team’s backend overhaul, Per Mertesacker will be joining as the managing director for the DFB from January 2027. He will be bringing vital experience as a World Cup winner and youth coach after spending over 8 years at the helm of Arsenal’s youth academy. The DFB announced Mertesacker’s appointment on Friday. He will be succeeding Andreas Rettig, whose contract expires at the end of this year.

news.title: World Cup Patches and the Future of Football Collectibles
news.lede: The World Cup has undergone several changes in various areas. From squads featuring all 26 players to referee cameras, dynamic ticket pricing, official FIFA reselling, partnerships with platforms like TikTok and YouTube, and hydration breaks, among others. However, there is another small change that is going to have a massive impact on a market rarely explored by football (soccer). Since 2010, FIFA has identified the reigning champion with a commemorative patch on the front of their jersey.

news.title: Kazuyoshi Miura: World's oldest professional footballer, 59, scores first goal in nearly four years
news.lede: Miura scored 55 goals for Japan, winning his last cap in 2000. Kazuyoshi Miura, the world's oldest professional footballer, scored his first goal in nearly four years at the age of 59 for Japanese third-tier side Fukushima United. Miura found the net in the 52nd minute to make it 5-0 to Fukushima in an eventual 7-0 win over Iwaki Furukawa in the Emperor's Cup on Saturday. It is his first competitive goal since netting for Suzuka PG, now Atletico Suzuka, against FC Osaka in November 2022.
